title: Resilient usage-event demultiplexer and progressive schema validator for Console pipelines
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Background: Console backend receives high-throughput usage events (API calls, token-level telemetry, embedding usage) from hosted and dedicated customers. Current ingestion is brittle for schema drift and bursts: malformed payloads cause downstream job failures, and synchronous rejects increase client latency and error rates. Goal: introduce a resilient demultiplexer service that routes incoming usage events into typed pipelines and a progressive validator that applies fast heuristics, best-effort repairs, and staged strict validation. This ticket scopes the core service, integration points, and fallbacks (dead-letter, metrics, and graceful degradation). Non-goals: redesigning downstream analytics consumers or changing storage schema for events (handled in separate migration tickets).
acceptance_criteria: New demultiplexer service accepts HTTP+gRPC ingest and forwards to typed internal topics (usage-raw, usage-lite, usage-validated) with <5ms median routing overhead
Progressive validator performs a quick syntactic/field-presence pass in the hot path and marks records with validation level (ok/warn/error) before enqueueing
Malformed events are not dropped synchronously: they are shunted to a dead-letter queue with reason codes and sample payloads stored for 30 days
Pipeline emits observability metrics: validation_error_rate, repaired_count, dlq_rate, average_route_latency and exposes them to Console dashboards
Integration tests cover 3 drift scenarios: missing fields, unexpected nested arrays, and token-count mismatch; consumer-side acceptance remains stable
Rollout strategy supports canary at 5% traffic and automatic rollback on elevated DLQ_rate or error budget burn
Documentation and runbook for on-call with triage steps and how to inspect repaired samples are added to Confluence
Security review completed for telemetry handling and PII-safe retention settings
implementation_notes: Create a new stateless service 'event-demux' behind the existing ingest ALB; support both JSON-over-HTTP and gRPC proto for high-throughput clients
Demux logic: lightweight header-based routing first (customer-tier, event-type), fallback to schema sniffing using a compact schema registry cache
Progressive validator stages: (1) fast schema fingerprint + required-field check; (2) heuristic repairs (string->number coercion, timestamp normalization); (3) strict schema check asynchronously
Use Kafka topics namespaced by customer when routing to downstream consumers; add TTL and compacted index on usage-validated topic
Dead-letter store: S3 prefix per day with manifest + small sample index in DynamoDB for fast lookup from Console

Backpressure approach: when downstream write latency exceeds threshold, demux buffers in bounded in-memory ring and starts shedding non-critical verbose telemetry with rate-limited sampling and emits shed_count metric
Expose health and metrics via /metrics and integrate with existing tracing (jaeger) for end-to-end latency breakdown
Add feature flag gating (ff: demux_progressive_validator) for staged rollout and quick disable
testing_plan: Unit tests for routing heuristics and schema cache expiration
Integration tests: run full ingest -> demux -> validator -> downstream consumer using test harness with synthetic drifted payloads
Chaos test: simulate downstream Kafka outage and verify DLQ behaviour, bounded buffering, and metric alerts
Performance test: 10k events/sec sustained profile with 95th percentile routing latency target <50ms
Security test: static analysis of new service, validate S3/DynamoACLs and KMS encryption settings
rollout_plan: Stage 1: Deploy to staging, validate metrics and integration tests
Stage 2: Enable canary at 5% traffic (region us-west-2), monitor DLQ_rate and route_latency for 24h
Stage 3: Ramp to 25% if canary stable for 24h, run load tests
Stage 4: Full roll after 72h stability and sign-off from SRE and Product
Rollback condition: sustained DLQ_rate > 0.5% for 2 hours or increase in error budget burn > 20% vs baseline
